items.note: Place 非常 directly before an adjective to express a high degree. It modifies the adjective, not the whole clause, so putting it after the adjective is incorrect.

items.wrongPy: tā men hǎo fēi cháng
items.why: 非常 must come before the adjective; the correct sentence is 她们非常好。

items.wrongPy: hàn yǔ hǎo fēi cháng
items.why: 非常 must come before the adjective; the correct sentence is 汉语非常好。

items.note: 和 joins noun phrases, such as two foods or two activities named as nouns; it does not normally join two complete clauses. Use it between the items being grouped. Learners often put 和 between a subject and verb, or treat it like English clause-level “and.”

items.wrongPy: wǒ xǐ huan hé shuǐ chá
items.why: 和 belongs between the noun phrases 水 and 茶; say 我喜欢水和茶。

items.en: In the afternoon I drink tea and water.
items.wrongPy: xià wǔ wǒ hé hē chá shuǐ
items.why: 和 cannot join the subject 我 to the verb phrase 喝茶; say 下午我喝茶和水。

items.note: Place 呢 after a person or thing when asking a contextual follow-up, such as “What about the teacher?” It is not placed before the noun. Learners may confuse this follow-up question with a question word; here, 呢 comes last.

items.wrongPy: ne nín
items.why: 呢 follows the person being asked about; the correct question is 您呢？

items.wrongPy: ne lǎo shī
items.why: 呢 must come after 老师, so the correct follow-up is 老师呢？

items.wrongPy: ne tóng xué
items.why: The noun comes before 呢 in this follow-up; the correct question is 同学呢？

items.en: What about a cup of tea?
items.wrongPy: yì bēi ne chá
items.why: 呢 cannot split the measure phrase from its noun here; the correct follow-up is 一杯茶呢？

items.wrongPy: hàn yǔ ne lǎo shī
items.why: 呢 follows the complete noun phrase; the correct question is 汉语老师呢？

items.note: These are complete, context-dependent utterances even without a full subject–predicate sentence. Use the expression or conversational sequence as given; learners sometimes reorder pieces that cannot move freely.

items.wrongPy: bàn liù diǎn
items.why: The time expression puts the hour before 半; say 六点半, not 半六点.

items.wrongPy: méi shì nǐ men ba shàng kè
items.why: 吧 follows the clause; the correct order is 你们上课吧.

items.en: You're welcome. You all get some rest.
items.wrongPy: bú kè qi nǐ men xiū xi dōu ba
items.why: 都 goes before 休息 and 吧 follows the clause; say 你们都休息吧.

items.note: Put 半 after 点 to express half past the stated hour. The hour comes first, followed by 点 and 半. Learners sometimes move 半 before 点 or place it after the activity instead of keeping the time expression together.

items.wrongPy: liù bàn diǎn
items.why: 半 must follow 点, so the correct time expression is 六点半.

items.en: Get up at half past nine.
items.wrongPy: jiǔ diǎn qǐ chuáng bàn
items.why: 半 belongs after 点 and before 起床, not after the activity.

items.en: My younger brother goes to work at half past nine.
items.wrongPy: dì di jiǔ diǎn shàng bān bàn
items.why: 半 must stay in the time expression 九点半, before 上班.

items.note: Form numbers from 10 to 99 with a tens digit before 十 and an optional ones digit after it. In 10–19, omit initial 一; learners often add it or reverse the digits.

items.en: My younger brother is ten years old.
items.wrongPy: dì di yì shí suì
items.why: For ten, omit initial 一; the correct age is 弟弟十岁。

items.wrongPy: wǒ yǒu yì shí gè xiǎo shí
items.why: Ten is 十, not 一十; say 我有十个小时。

items.en: My younger brother is twenty this year.
items.wrongPy: dì di jīn nián shí suì èr
items.why: The tens digit must precede 十 and the ones digit follow it; say 弟弟今年二十岁。

items.note: Put 谁, 什么, 哪儿, or 哪里 in the sentence slot for the answer being asked about. These question words do not need 吗; learners often put them in the wrong slot or add 吗.

items.wrongPy: nǎr māo zài
items.why: 哪儿 belongs after 在 here; say 猫在哪儿？

items.wrongPy: shéi gōng sī zài
items.why: 谁 belongs in the subject slot before 在公司; the correct question is 谁在公司？

items.wrongPy: nǎ lǐ píng guǒ zài
items.why: 哪里 follows 在 in this question; say 苹果在哪里？

items.wrongPy: hái zi shén me yào
items.why: 什么 follows 要 as its object; the correct order is 孩子要什么？

items.en: Who is going to the bookstore to buy books?
items.wrongPy: shéi shū diàn qù mǎi shū
items.why: 谁 must occupy the subject slot before 去; say 谁去书店买书？

items.en: When are you going to the bookstore?
items.wrongPy: nǐ shén me shí hou shū diàn qù
items.why: 什么时候 belongs before 去书店; say 你什么时候去书店？

items.note: A basic statement places the subject first and the predicate after it. Use this pattern to say what someone does, what something is like, or where something is. Learners sometimes reverse the subject and predicate; keep the person or thing being described at the beginning.

items.wrongPy: xué xí nǐ
items.why: The subject must come first; say 你学习。

items.wrongPy: hěn hǎo mǐ fàn
items.why: The subject 米饭 must precede its predicate 很好。

items.wrongPy: fēi cháng hǎo tā men
items.why: 她们 is the subject and must come before 非常好。

items.note: Use 是 before a noun to identify or classify the subject, as in saying who someone is or what something is. The noun follows 是. A common error is moving 是 or the noun before the subject; keep the order subject + 是 + noun.

items.wrongPy: shì zhè shì wǒ
items.why: 是 must follow the subject 这; the correct order is 这是我。

items.wrongPy: shì xué sheng zhè
items.why: 这 must be the subject before 是学生, not follow 是。

items.wrongPy: nǐ ma shì lǎo shī
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the question; say 你是老师吗？

items.wrongPy: tā men shì dōu dà xué shēng
items.why: 都 comes before 是; say 她们都是大学生。

items.note: Put 都 after a plural subject or quantified group and before the predicate to say every member shares the same situation. Learners often place 都 after the verb; that order is wrong here.

items.wrongPy: wǒ men xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 belongs before the predicate; the correct sentence is 我们都休息。

items.en: They are all nine years old.
items.wrongPy: tā men jiǔ suì dōu
items.why: 都 must precede the predicate; the correct sentence is 她们都九岁。

items.wrongPy: tā men shì dà xué shēng dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate; the correct sentence is 她们都是大学生。

items.wrongPy: wǔ gè tóng xué xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate; the correct sentence is 五个同学都休息。

items.en: These primary school students are all very busy.
items.wrongPy: zhè xiē xiǎo xué shēng hěn máng dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate; the correct sentence is 这些小学生都很忙。

items.en: All four daughters are very happy.
items.wrongPy: sì gè nǚ ér hěn gāo xìng dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate; the correct sentence is 四个女儿都很高兴。

items.note: Put a descriptive adjective phrase before the noun, usually linking it with 的; some short, fixed combinations omit 的. Use 的 especially when the description is longer. Learners often leave it out after an adjective phrase containing 很.

items.en: The new clothes are very good.
items.wrongPy: hěn xīn yī fu hěn hǎo
items.why: 很新 is an adjective phrase modifying 衣服, so it needs 的; the correct phrase is 很新的衣服。

items.wrongPy: hěn dà fáng jiān hěn xīn
items.why: 很大 needs 的 before 房间; say 很大的房间。

items.en: I want to buy cheap things.
items.wrongPy: pián yi de wǒ xiǎng mǎi dōng xi
items.why: The modifier must precede the noun it describes; say 我想买便宜的东西。

items.phrase: 这家商店卖便宜的东西
items.zh: 这家商店卖便宜的东西。
items.wrong: 这家商店卖东西的便宜。
items.wrongPy: zhè jiā shāng diàn mài dōng xi de pián yi
items.why: 的 belongs between 便宜 and 东西, not after 东西; say 这家商店卖便宜的东西。

items.note: In a noun-noun modifier, the first noun specifies the type or topic of the second noun, with no 的 in these examples. Use the order modifier + head noun. Learners sometimes reverse the nouns, which changes or breaks the intended noun phrase.

items.wrongPy: lǎo shī hàn yǔ ne
items.why: 汉语 specifies the kind of 老师, so it must come first: 汉语老师。

items.wrongPy: yī shēng nǚ hěn máng
items.why: 女 modifies 医生 and must precede it: 女医生很忙。

items.wrongPy: wǒ xǐ huan gē zhōng guó
items.why: 中国 modifies 歌 and must come first: 中国歌。

items.wrongPy: rén zhōng guó xǐ huan dú shū
items.why: 中国 modifies 人, so the noun phrase must be 中国人。

items.wrongPy: lǎo shī hàn yǔ xué xí hàn yǔ
items.why: 汉语 must precede 老师 in this noun phrase: 汉语老师。

items.note: Use 有没有 to ask whether someone has something; 没有 is the negative form of 有. Do not replace 没 with 不, a common mistake because English uses “not have.”

items.wrongPy: nǐ bù yǒu jiǎo zi
items.why: 不有 is not the negative form of 有; ask 你有没有饺子？

items.wrongPy: nǐ bù yǒu xīn yī fu
items.why: 不有 is not the negative form of 有; ask 你有没有新衣服？

items.note: Use 太 before an adjective and 了 at the end to express an extreme degree, often “so” or “too.” It describes the situation, not a past event; learners often mistake 了 here for a past-tense marker.

items.wrongPy: xiàn zài máng tài le
items.why: 太 must precede the adjective, so say 现在太忙了。

items.wrongPy: xiàn zài shí jiān wǎn tài le
items.why: 太 must come before 晚, so say 现在时间太晚了。

items.wrongPy: zhè jiā shāng diàn pián yi tài le
items.why: 太 must precede the adjective, so say 这家商店太便宜了！

items.en: This piece of clothing is so good-looking!
items.wrongPy: zhè jiàn yī fu hǎo kàn tài le
items.why: 太 must precede the adjective, so say 这件衣服太好看了！

items.note: Put the number before 杯 and the drink noun after it to count cupfuls. 杯 is the measure word here, not the container noun 杯子; learners should not insert another measure word between the number and 杯.

items.en: What about a cup of tea?
items.wrongPy: yí gè bēi chá ne
items.why: 个 cannot go between the number and 杯; the correct phrase is 一杯茶呢？

items.en: I’d like three cups of tea.
items.wrongPy: yào sān gè bēi chá
items.why: 个 is not used with 杯 in this measure phrase; the correct version is 要三杯茶.

items.en: I’d like half a cup of tea.
items.wrongPy: yào bàn gè bēi chá
items.why: 半杯 is the correct measure phrase, not 半个杯; say 要半杯茶.

items.en: She has a cup of tea.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu yí gè bēi chá
items.why: 个 cannot be added before 杯 here; the correct phrase is 她有一杯茶.

items.en: I want a cup of milk.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yào yí gè bēi niú nǎi
items.why: 个 does not belong between 一 and 杯; the correct phrase is 我要一杯牛奶.

items.en: They drink five cups of milk.
items.wrongPy: tā men hē wǔ gè bēi niú nǎi
items.why: Use 五杯, not 五个杯, to count cupfuls; the correct phrase is 她们喝五杯牛奶.

items.note: Put a number before a measure word and the noun: 两本书, 一个苹果. Choose a measure word that fits the noun, and do not leave it out in an ordinary counted noun phrase. Learners often omit the measure word or put it in the wrong position.

items.en: The two books are very good.
items.wrongPy: běn liǎng shū hěn hǎo
items.why: The number must precede the measure word and noun; say 两本书.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yǒu yì píng guǒ
items.why: A measure word is needed between 一 and 苹果; say 一个苹果.

items.en: There are four people in her family.
items.wrongPy: tā jiā yǒu sì běn rén
items.why: 本 counts books, not people; use 口 for 人 here.

items.en: All three rooms are very nice.
items.wrongPy: sān gè dōu fáng jiān hěn hǎo
items.why: 都 must follow the subject phrase, not split the measure phrase; say 三个房间都很好.

items.en: All four children are very happy.
items.wrongPy: sì gè dōu hái zi hěn gāo xìng
items.why: 都 follows the complete subject phrase; say 四个孩子都很高兴.

items.note: State someone's age with the person followed by the number and 岁; no 是 is needed. When included, 今年 usually comes before the age. Learners may wrongly add the measure word 个 before 岁, or put 岁 before the number.

items.en: My younger brother is three years old.
items.wrongPy: dì di suì sān
items.why: The number must come before 岁: 弟弟三岁.

items.en: She is nine years old this year.
items.wrongPy: tā jiǔ suì jīn nián
items.why: 今年 belongs before the age expression, not after it.

items.en: They are all nine years old.
items.wrongPy: tā men jiǔ suì dōu
items.why: 都 belongs before the age predicate, as in 她们都九岁.

items.en: My younger brother is nine this year.
items.wrongPy: dì di jīn nián suì jiǔ
items.why: The number must come before 岁: 弟弟今年九岁.

items.en: My younger brother is twenty this year.
items.wrongPy: dì di jīn nián èr shí gè suì
items.why: Age uses 二十岁 without 个; 个 cannot be inserted before 岁.

items.note: Place 对 plus the addressee before the speech verb phrase to show whom someone speaks to. Use this with compatible speech actions such as saying something or speaking a language. Learners often put 对 after the speech verb; the addressee comes before it.

items.en: I want to say thank you to her.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xiǎng duì shuō tā xiè xie
items.why: The addressee must follow 对 and come before 说; here 说 comes too early.

items.en: She speaks Chinese to her boyfriend.
items.wrongPy: tā duì shuō nán péng you hàn yǔ
items.why: The person addressed must immediately follow 对 and precede the speech verb phrase.

items.en: The son said to the doctor, “I’m sick.”
items.wrongPy: ér zi shuō duì yī shēng wǒ bìng le
items.why: 对医生 must come before 说, not after it.

items.phrase: 妈妈对儿子说去商店吧
items.zh: 妈妈对儿子说：“去商店吧。”
items.en: Mom says to her son, “Let’s go to the shop.”
items.wrong: 妈妈对说儿子：“去商店吧。”
items.wrongPy: mā ma duì shuō ér zi qù shāng diàn ba
items.why: The addressee must follow 对 before the speech verb 说.

items.phrase: 哥哥对妈妈说饺子便宜
items.zh: 哥哥对妈妈说饺子便宜。
items.en: Older brother tells Mom the dumplings are cheap.
items.wrong: 哥哥说对妈妈饺子便宜。
items.wrongPy: gē ge shuō duì mā ma jiǎo zi pián yi
items.why: The addressee phrase 对妈妈 must precede the speech verb 说.

items.note: Additive 还 introduces another fact or action and normally comes before the predicate, often after an optional repeated subject. Use it to mean “also”; it can mean “still” in other contexts, so learners should not assume every 还 is additive.

items.en: They cook and also drink tea.
items.wrongPy: tā men zuò fàn hē hái chá
items.why: 还 must come before the predicate, not between 喝 and 茶; the correct order is 她们做饭，还喝茶。

items.en: They drink tea and also drink water.
items.wrongPy: tā men hē chá hē shuǐ hái
items.why: 还 must precede the added predicate, not follow it; say 她们喝茶，还喝水。

items.phrase: 妹妹会写汉字还会做饭
items.zh: 妹妹会写汉字，还会做饭。
items.en: My younger sister can write Chinese characters, and she can also cook.
items.wrong: 妹妹会写汉字，还做饭会。
items.wrongPy: mèi mei huì xiě hàn zì hái zuò fàn huì
items.why: 还 must precede the predicate 会做饭; say 妹妹会写汉字，还会做饭。

items.note: Put 对 before the person or thing that receives the attitude, then state the attitude. Use this pattern for how someone treats or feels about someone; learners often put 对 after the attitude.

items.en: Mom is very nice to my older brother.
items.wrongPy: mā ma gē ge duì hěn hǎo
items.why: 对 must come before 哥哥, so say 妈妈对哥哥很好。

items.en: The younger sister is very kind to Dad.
items.wrongPy: mèi mei hěn hǎo duì bà ba
items.why: 对爸爸 must come before the attitude, so say 妹妹对爸爸很好。

items.en: Dad is very kind to my younger sister.
items.wrongPy: bà ba duì hěn hǎo mèi mei
items.why: 妹妹 must follow 对 before the attitude, so say 爸爸对妹妹很好。

items.note: Final 呢 can mark an action as ongoing when the context makes that reading clear. 在 may come before the verb phrase, but it is not required. Learners often put 呢 before the action instead of at the end.

items.wrongPy: bà ba ne shuì jiào
items.why: 呢 belongs at the end to mark the ongoing action, not between the subject and verb.

items.wrongPy: gē ge hái ne shuì jiào
items.why: 呢 should follow the verb phrase, not come between 还 and 睡觉.

items.en: Big sister is sleeping at home.
items.wrongPy: jiě jie zài shuì jiào jiā ne
items.why: The location 在家 must come before the verb phrase, not after 睡觉.

items.wrongPy: mā ma zài jiā ne zuò fàn
items.why: 呢 marks the ongoing action at the end, not between the location and the verb.

items.note: Use 有些 or 有的 before a noun to identify a subset, then state its predicate. 有的 can also stand alone when the noun is understood. Learners often put the predicate before the noun, but here the noun must immediately follow 有些 or 有的.

items.wrongPy: yǒu xiē péng you shū yǒu
items.why: The noun must follow 有些; put 朋友 before the predicate 有书.

items.wrongPy: yǒu de péng you shū yǒu
items.why: The noun must follow 有的; put 朋友 before the predicate 有书.

items.wrongPy: yǒu xiē hěn shuǐ guǒ guì
items.why: 有些 must directly precede its noun, so put 水果 before the predicate 很贵.

items.en: Some cats are behind the table.
items.wrongPy: yǒu de māo zài hòu biān zhuō zi
items.why: The location phrase is 在桌子后边, not 在后边桌子.

items.phrase: 有些孩子在超市外边玩
items.zh: 有些孩子在超市外边玩。
items.en: Some children are playing outside the supermarket.
items.wrong: 有些孩子在超市玩外边。
items.wrongPy: yǒu xiē hái zi zài chāo shì wán wài bian
items.why: The location must come before 玩; say 在超市外边玩.

items.note: 不要 comes before a verb phrase to tell someone not to do something. Keep the whole action after 不要. Learners may move a verb or location around and leave the sentence without a grammatical structure.

items.wrongPy: bú yào shuì jiào zài
items.why: 在 cannot trail 睡觉 without a location; the correct prohibition is 不要睡觉。

items.wrongPy: bú yào chàng gē zài
items.why: 在 cannot trail 唱歌 without a location; the correct prohibition is 不要唱歌。

items.wrongPy: bú yào diàn nǎo kāi
items.why: 开电脑 is the verb-object phrase, so the object cannot come before 开 here.

items.wrongPy: bú yào zài shuō huà diàn yǐng yuàn
items.why: The location phrase 在电影院 must come before 说话, not split by the verb.

items.note: Put 呢 after a person or thing to ask where they or it is, usually when the context makes the search clear. Learners may mistake this for an ongoing-action sentence; here 呢 follows a noun, not a verb phrase.

items.wrongPy: ne mèi mei
items.why: For a where question, 呢 follows the person or thing; it cannot come before 妹妹.

items.wrongPy: ne diàn yǐng yuàn
items.why: For a where question, 呢 follows the person or thing; it cannot come before 电影院.

items.note: Here 还 means “also” or “in addition” and comes before the predicate it adds. It does not mean “still” in these examples. Learners often place 还 after the verb instead of before the whole predicate.

items.en: The dog is also looking for steamed buns.
items.wrongPy: gǒu zhǎo hái bāo zi
items.why: 还 must come before the predicate 找包子; the correct order is 狗还找包子。

items.en: She has a phone, and she also has a computer.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu shǒu jī tā yǒu hái diàn nǎo
items.why: 还 must come before the predicate 有电脑, not between 有 and 电脑.

items.note: Put 这些 or 那些 directly before the noun to mean these or those. The demonstrative phrase can then be the subject of a sentence. Learners often put the noun first, but the demonstrative must precede it here.

items.wrongPy: shū zhè xiē bù xīn
items.why: 这些 must precede its noun, so say 这些书不新.

items.wrongPy: cài zhè xiē hěn hǎo
items.why: 这些 must precede its noun, so say 这些菜很好.

items.wrongPy: gǒu zhè xiē zài jiā
items.why: 这些 must precede its noun, so say 这些狗在家.

items.wrongPy: hái zi nà xiē hěn gāo xìng
items.why: 那些 must precede its noun, so say 那些孩子很高兴.

items.wrongPy: shuǐ guǒ nà xiē hěn pián yi
items.why: 那些 must precede its noun, so say 那些水果很便宜.

items.wrongPy: hàn zì zhè xiē hěn hǎo kàn
items.why: 这些 must precede its noun, so say 这些汉字很好看.

items.note: With a double-object verb such as 给, put the person after the verb and before the thing: 给弟弟两本书. Learners often put the thing first, copying English word order; keep the person before the thing.

items.en: I invite you to eat steamed buns.
items.wrongPy: wǒ qǐng chī bāo zi nǐ
items.why: The person invited comes before the action; say 我请你吃包子.

items.en: I give my younger brother two books.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gěi liǎng běn shū dì di
items.why: The person comes before the thing after 给; say 我给弟弟两本书.

items.en: My younger brother gives me two apples.
items.wrongPy: dì di gěi liǎng gè píng guǒ wǒ
items.why: The person comes before the thing after 给; say 弟弟给我两个苹果.

items.note: A basic verbal statement puts the subject before the verb phrase and does not use 是 before an ordinary action verb. Use this pattern for actions and activities. Learners sometimes move the object before the verb or place 都 after the verb; keep the usual order.

items.wrongPy: tīng wǒ gē
items.why: The subject must precede the verb phrase; the correct sentence is 我听歌。

items.wrongPy: dú tā hàn zì
items.why: The subject comes before the verb and object; the correct sentence is 他读汉字。

items.wrongPy: tā men xiū xi dōu
items.why: 都 comes before the verb it modifies; the correct sentence is 她们都休息。

items.wrongPy: xué xí lǎo shī hàn yǔ
items.why: The subject must come before the verb phrase; the correct sentence is 老师学习汉语。

items.wrongPy: xià wǔ xiū xi wǒ men ba
items.why: The subject comes before 休息; the correct sentence is 下午我们休息吧。

items.wrongPy: wǒ men diàn yǐng yuàn qù ba
items.why: 电影院 comes after 去, not before it; the correct sentence is 我们去电影院吧。

items.note: Put 会 after the subject and before a verb phrase to describe a learned skill or ability. It does not simply mean general possibility or permission. Learners often move 会 to the end of the verb phrase; it belongs before the skill verb.

items.wrongPy: huì tā kāi chē
items.why: 会 belongs after the subject 他 and before the skill verb phrase.

items.en: My younger brother is good at studying.
items.wrongPy: huì dì di dú shū
items.why: 会 must come after the subject, not before it.

items.wrongPy: huì wǒ zuò wǎn fàn
items.why: 会 must follow 我 and precede the verb phrase.

items.en: My younger sister can make dumplings.
items.wrongPy: huì mèi mei zuò jiǎo zi
items.why: 会 must come after the subject 妹妹, not before it.

items.note: 真 goes before an adjective to give an emphatic evaluation, often with an exclamation. Use it to say that something is really or truly a certain way. Learners sometimes put 真 after the adjective or between a verb and adjective.

items.wrongPy: gǒu xiǎo zhēn
items.why: 真 must precede 小; the correct emphatic sentence is 狗真小！

items.wrongPy: bāo zi zhēn chī hǎo
items.why: 真 modifies 好吃 and must precede the adjective phrase; the correct sentence is 包子真好吃！

items.en: My younger sister is really happy!
items.wrongPy: mèi mei gāo xìng zhēn
items.why: 真 must come before 高兴; the correct emphatic sentence is 妹妹真高兴！

items.en: The TV show is really enjoyable to watch!
items.wrongPy: diàn shì hǎo kàn zhēn
items.why: 真 must precede 好看; the correct sentence is 电视真好看！

items.en: This book is really enjoyable to read!
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū hǎo kàn zhēn
items.why: 真 must precede 好看; the correct sentence is 这本书真好看！

items.note: 喂 is a conventional greeting used when answering or starting a phone call. Put the question particle 吗 at the end of the question, not immediately after its subject; the greeting itself does not change the question’s word order.

items.wrongPy: wéi tā men ma zài jiā
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the question, not after 他们; say 喂？他们在家吗？

items.wrongPy: wéi bà ba ma zài jiā
items.why: 吗 belongs at the end of the question, not after 爸爸; say 喂？爸爸在家吗？

items.note: Use 再 before the verb phrase for a repeated action that is still future or intended, often with a time expression. Learners wrongly put 再 after the verb or its object; it belongs before the whole verb phrase.

items.wrongPy: tā men míng tiān lái zài
items.why: 再 must precede 来, so the correct order is 他们明天再来。

items.en: Tomorrow we’ll go to the bookstore again.
items.wrongPy: míng tiān wǒ men qù zài shū diàn
items.why: 再 must precede the whole verb phrase 去书店, so the correct order is 明天我们再去书店。

items.en: Let’s go to the bookstore again tomorrow.
items.wrongPy: míng tiān wǒ men qù shū diàn zài ba
items.why: 再 must precede 去书店, so the correct order is 明天我们再去书店吧。

items.note: Put 有 after the subject to say that someone possesses something or that something exists in a time or place frame. Put the possessed or existing noun phrase after 有. Learners often put that noun phrase before 有, reversing the usual order.

items.wrongPy: tā niú nǎi yǒu
items.why: The noun phrase follows 有 in this pattern; say 她有牛奶.

items.wrongPy: zuó tiān wèn tí yǒu
items.why: The existing noun phrase follows 有; say 昨天有问题.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yí gè péng you yǒu
items.why: The possessed noun phrase follows 有; say 我有一个朋友.

items.wrongPy: wǒ shí gè xiǎo shí yǒu
items.why: The possessed noun phrase follows 有; say 我有十个小时.

items.en: There are four people in her family.
items.wrongPy: tā jiā sì kǒu rén yǒu
items.why: The existing noun phrase follows 有; say 她家有四口人.

items.en: The son is ill and needs to go to the hospital.
items.wrongPy: ér zi bìng yǒu
items.why: 病 follows 有 in this expression; say 儿子有病.

items.note: Use 这 or 那 followed by a measure word and then the noun. The measure word depends on the noun, so learners should not replace it with a different classifier just because another one is familiar or common.

items.wrongPy: nà běn shāng diàn hěn dà
items.why: 商店 takes 家 here, not 本; say 那家商店很大。

items.wrongPy: zhè ge běn wèn tí hěn dà
items.why: This stacks two measure words; use just 个, as in 这个问题很大。

items.en: That new item of clothing looks very nice.
items.wrongPy: nà běn xīn yī fu hěn hǎo kàn
items.why: 衣服 takes 件 here, not 本; say 那件新衣服很好看。

items.note: In spoken prices, a digit after 块 gives tenths of a yuan: 八块五 means 8.50 yuan. Learners often add 分, which makes the final digit hundredths instead, changing the price to 8.05 yuan.

For thousands, place the thousands digit before 千, then put any remainder after 千; keep the initial 一 when the amount requires it. Learners may reverse the digit and 千, producing an invalid number expression.

items.en: This book costs three thousand yuan.
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū qiān sān yuán
items.why: The digit must precede 千; say 这本书三千元。

items.en: That book costs four thousand yuan.
items.wrongPy: nà běn shū qiān sì yuán
items.why: The digit must precede 千; say 那本书四千元。

items.note: A nominal predicate places a subject before a noun-like description, especially for age, dates, and prices when context makes the relationship clear. Learners may wrongly add 是 everywhere or use 不 directly; negative nominal predicates generally need 不是.

items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū shí gè kuài
items.why: 个 is not used between a price amount and 块 here; say 这本书十块。

items.wrongPy: míng tiān bù xīng qī rì
items.why: A nominal predicate cannot be negated directly with 不; say 明天不是星期日。

items.en: This book is eight yuan fifty.
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū bā wǔ kuài
items.why: The currency unit must follow the amount; say 这本书八块五。

items.en: This book costs three thousand yuan.
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū yuán sān qiān
items.why: The amount must precede 元; say 这本书三千元。

items.en: This book costs two yuan and three fen.
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū liǎng yuán fēn sān
items.why: The amount must precede its currency unit; say 这本书两元三分。

items.note: Chinese clock times put the hour before 点 and the minutes before 分; an exact hour can omit the minutes. Add a time-of-day word when needed. Learners often reverse the hour and minutes: the hour must come first, even when both numbers are written out.

For a number in the hundreds, say the hundreds digit, then 百, then any remainder. Keep 一 in 一百, but omit a trailing zero rather than saying it. Learners sometimes put the unit 百 after the remainder; 百 must follow the hundreds digit.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yǒu yuán bǎi wǔ
items.why: 百 must follow the hundreds digit, not come after the remainder; say 我有五百元。

items.en: There are seven hundred yuan there.
items.wrongPy: nàr yǒu yuán bǎi qī
items.why: 百 must follow the hundreds digit, not come after the remainder; say 那儿有七百元。

items.note: Put 要 after the subject and before a verb phrase to express wanting, needing, or intending to act; it can also mark an imminent event. Learners often put 要 after the verb, or confuse it with 想 in every context.

items.en: He wants to see a doctor.
items.wrongPy: tā kàn bìng yào
items.why: 要 belongs before the verb phrase 看病, not after it.

items.wrongPy: jīn tiān xià yǔ yào le
items.why: 要 must precede the verb phrase 下雨 in this imminent-event construction.

items.en: The male doctor is going to return to the hospital.
items.wrongPy: nán yī shēng huí yī yuàn yào
items.why: 要 must precede the verb phrase 回医院.

items.en: The son is ill and needs to go to the hospital.
items.wrongPy: ér zi bù yǒu bìng yào qù yī yuàn
items.why: 不 cannot directly negate 有; the negation form for 有 uses a different word.

items.note: Put 想 after the subject and before the verb phrase to express wanting or intending to do something. The verb phrase can include other elements, but learners commonly place 想 after the main verb instead of before the whole action.

items.en: I want to learn to cook.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xué xiǎng zuò cài
items.why: 想 must come before the action 学做菜; say 我想学做菜。

items.en: The son wants to go home.
items.wrongPy: ér zi huí jiā xiǎng
items.why: 想 precedes the action 回家, not follows it; say 儿子想回家。

items.en: It wants to go live there.
items.wrongPy: tā qù nàr xiǎng zhù
items.why: 想 must precede the whole action 去那儿住; say 它想去那儿住。

items.wrongPy: mā ma zuò xiǎng jiǎo zi
items.why: 想 comes before the verb phrase 做饺子; say 妈妈想做饺子。

items.en: The daughter wants to live in China.
items.wrongPy: nǚ ér zhù xiǎng zài zhōng guó
items.why: 想 must precede the action 住在中国; say 女儿想住在中国。

items.en: Next year I want to study at the university.
items.wrongPy: míng nián wǒ xiǎng dú shū zài dà xué
items.why: The location 在大学 belongs before the verb 读书; say 明年我想在大学读书。

items.note: Use 两 before a measure word when counting two ordinary things, as in 两杯茶 and 两本书. Use 二 for digits, ordinals, and numbers such as twenty. Learners often put 两 after the measure word or leave the measure word out; keep the order 两 + measure word + noun.

items.wrongPy: bēi liǎng chá
items.why: 两 must come before 杯; the correct order is 两杯茶.

items.wrongPy: māo yǒu liǎng běn péng you
items.why: 本 counts books, not friends; use 个 for 朋友.

items.wrongPy: hái zi yǒu liǎng shū běn
items.why: The measure word must come between 两 and 书; say 两本书.

items.en: I buy two pieces of bread.
items.wrongPy: wǒ mǎi liǎng běn miàn bāo
items.why: 本 counts books, not pieces of bread; use 块 for 面包.

items.en: I give my younger brother two books.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gěi dì di shū liǎng běn
items.why: The measure phrase must precede the noun; say 两本书.

items.note: Two verb phrases share one subject: the first describes the means, and the second gives the main action or destination. Use this when explaining how someone gets somewhere or does something. Keep the means phrase together before the main action; learners often misplace its object.

items.en: I take a car to school.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zuò qù chē shàng xué
items.why: 坐车 must stay together before 去; the correct order is 我坐车去上学。

items.en: He takes a car to the restaurant.
items.wrongPy: tā zuò qù chē fàn diàn
items.why: 坐车 must stay together before 去; the correct order is 他坐车去饭店。

items.en: She takes a car to see a movie.
items.wrongPy: tā zuò qù chē kàn diàn yǐng
items.why: 坐车 must stay together before 去; the correct order is 她坐车去看电影。

items.note: 和 joins the subject with the person who does the action alongside them, and the shared verb phrase follows both people. Learners may place 和 before the action instead of between the two people; it must connect people, not a person and a verb phrase.

items.en: My girlfriend and I take the train.
items.wrongPy: wǒ nǚ péng you hé zuò huǒ chē
items.why: 和 must be followed by the other person, not the action; say 我和女朋友坐火车.

items.note: 哪些 comes directly before the noun to ask which members of a group are meant. It already identifies multiple items, so it does not take an individual measure word here. Learners may mistakenly move 哪些 after the noun or add 个.

items.wrongPy: wèn tí nǎ xiē
items.why: 哪些 must come before 问题; the correct phrase is 哪些问题？

items.wrongPy: cài nǎ xiē hǎo chī
items.why: 哪些 must come before 菜; the correct question is 哪些菜好吃？

items.en: Which classes are in the morning?
items.wrongPy: kè nǎ xiē zài shàng wǔ
items.why: 哪些 must come before 课; the correct question is 哪些课在上午？

items.note: Some adjectives can come before a verb phrase to describe how the action is done; 快 before 上火车 or 上课 urges people to hurry. The construction depends on the adjective, so do not assume every adjective can be placed before every verb.

items.en: Everyone, hurry and get on the train.
items.wrongPy: dà jiā kuài ba shàng huǒ chē
items.why: 吧 cannot interrupt 快 and 上火车; put it after the action, as in 大家快上火车。

items.wrongPy: dà jiā kuài ba shàng kè
items.why: 吧 cannot interrupt 快 and 上课; put it after the action, as in 大家快上课吧。

items.note: Put 不 immediately before a predicate to negate a habit, intention, or description. It does not normally negate possession or a completed event. Learners often put 不 after the verb or object; keep it directly before the predicate instead.

items.wrongPy: bù yǔ dà
items.why: 不 must follow the subject and precede the predicate; the correct order is 雨不大。

items.wrongPy: wǒ bú nà ge yào
items.why: 不 precedes 要, not the object; the correct sentence is 我不要那个。

items.wrongPy: xīn zhè xiē shū bù
items.why: The subject must come before its predicate; the correct sentence is 这些书不新。

items.wrongPy: wǒ xué xí bú hàn yǔ
items.why: 不 must precede 学习, not separate the verb from its object; the correct sentence is 我不学习汉语。

items.wrongPy: bú zhè ge wèn tí dà
items.why: The subject must precede 不; the correct sentence is 这个问题不大。

items.en: This new item of clothing is not expensive.
items.wrongPy: zhè jiàn xīn yī fu guì bù
items.why: This leaves 不 after the predicate; the correct negative description is 这件新衣服不贵。

items.note: Place 也 before the predicate to add a parallel fact, and omit the repeated subject only when clear. Learners often put 也 after the verb or adjective instead.

items.en: Dad loves her, and she loves Dad too.
items.wrongPy: bà ba ài tā tā ài yě bà ba
items.why: 也 must come before the predicate 爱, so say 她也爱爸爸。

items.en: The older sister is young, and the younger sister is too.
items.wrongPy: jiě jie hěn xiǎo mèi mei hěn yě xiǎo
items.why: 也 must precede the predicate 很小, so say 妹妹也很小。

items.phrase: 妈妈做饺子爸爸也做饺子
items.zh: 妈妈做饺子，爸爸也做饺子。
items.en: Mom makes dumplings, and Dad does too.
items.wrong: 妈妈做饺子，爸爸做也饺子。
items.wrongPy: mā ma zuò jiǎo zi bà ba zuò yě jiǎo zi
items.why: 也 must come before 做, so say 爸爸也做饺子。

items.phrase: 我吃一半面包也吃一点儿饭
items.zh: 我吃一半面包，也吃一点儿饭。
items.en: I eat half a loaf of bread and also a little rice.
items.wrong: 我吃一半面包，吃也一点儿饭。
items.wrongPy: wǒ chī yí bàn miàn bāo chī yě yì diǎnr fàn
items.why: 也 must come before 吃, so say 也吃一点儿饭。

items.note: 怎么 comes before the verb phrase to ask how an action is performed. It is commonly followed by a verb, then its object, as in 怎么坐火车. Learners may mistakenly place 怎么 before the object instead of before the verb.

items.en: How do you take the train?
items.wrongPy: nǐ zuò zěn me huǒ chē
items.why: 怎么 must come before 坐, not between 坐 and 火车; say 你怎么坐火车？

items.en: How does everyone get to the restaurant?
items.wrongPy: dà jiā qù zěn me fàn diàn
items.why: 怎么 must come before 去, not between 去 and 饭店; say 大家怎么去饭店？

items.note: Use 一点儿 before a mass noun to express a small quantity. Learners often put it after the noun, as though it were a general amount complement; in this pattern it comes before the noun.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yào shuǐ yì diǎnr
items.why: 一点儿 must precede 水 here; the correct phrase is 我要一点儿水.

items.wrongPy: tā men yào mǐ fàn yì diǎnr
items.why: 一点儿 must precede 米饭 here; the correct phrase is 她们要一点儿米饭.

items.en: I drink a little milk in the evening.
items.wrongPy: wǎn shang wǒ hē niú nǎi yì diǎnr
items.why: 一点儿 must precede 牛奶 here; the correct phrase is 晚上我喝一点儿牛奶.

items.phrase: 我吃一半面包也吃一点儿饭
items.zh: 我吃一半面包，也吃一点儿饭。
items.en: I eat half a loaf of bread and also a little rice.
items.wrong: 我吃一半面包，也吃饭一点儿。
items.wrongPy: wǒ chī yí bàn miàn bāo yě chī fàn yì diǎnr
items.why: 一点儿 must precede 饭 here; the correct phrase is 我吃一半面包，也吃一点儿饭.

items.note: Put 有点儿 or 有一点儿 immediately before an adjective to mean somewhat, often with an undesirable feeling or quality. Learners often put it after the adjective, which is not grammatical.

items.wrongPy: tā lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 goes before 冷; the correct sentence is 她有点儿冷。

items.wrongPy: tā lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 goes before 冷; the correct sentence is 他有点儿冷。

items.en: The water is a little cold.
items.wrongPy: shuǐ lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 goes before 冷; the correct sentence is 水有点儿冷。

items.en: It is a little hot today.
items.wrongPy: jīn tiān rè yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 goes before 热; the correct sentence is 今天有点儿热。

items.en: This milk is a little cold.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge niú nǎi lěng yǒu diǎnr
items.why: 有点儿 goes before 冷; the correct sentence is 这个牛奶有点儿冷。

items.wrongPy: tā men jué de lěng yǒu yì diǎnr
items.why: 有一点儿 goes before 冷; the correct sentence is 她们觉得有一点儿冷。

items.note: Put 去 or 来 before the destination and the shared subject’s action after it, expressing movement for that purpose. The same person does both. Learners often reverse the destination and action; the place must come before the verb phrase.

items.en: She goes to the bookstore to buy books.
items.wrongPy: tā qù mǎi shū shū diàn
items.why: The destination must precede the action, so say 去书店买书.

items.en: She goes to primary school to study.
items.wrongPy: tā qù dú shū xiǎo xué
items.why: The destination must precede the action, so say 去小学读书.

items.en: I’m coming to the bookstore to buy books.
items.wrongPy: wǒ lái mǎi shū shū diàn
items.why: The destination must precede the action, so say 来书店买书.

items.en: I’ll drive to the restaurant after class.
items.wrongPy: wǒ xià kè hòu kāi chē fàn diàn qù
items.why: The destination must follow 去, so say 开车去饭店.

items.note: Some verb-object compounds can be split, with an aspect marker or quantity phrase placed between the verb and object, as in 上了课. Learners often put the marker before the whole compound. Not every compound allows this separation.

items.wrongPy: dà jiā le shàng kè
items.why: 了 belongs between 上 and 课; the correct sentence is 大家上了课。

items.phrase: 我们在下课后去看电影
items.zh: 我们在下课后去看电影。
items.en: We go to see a movie after class.
items.wrong: 我们在下后课去看电影。
items.wrongPy: wǒ men zài xià hòu kè qù kàn diàn yǐng
items.why: 后 follows the complete compound 下课; the correct sentence is 我们在下课后去看电影。

items.note: Verb + 了 + object marks a completed or bounded event; it does not by itself mean past tense. Use this order when the verb takes an object. Learners often place 了 before the verb or inside the object.

items.en: My younger sister ate a bun.
items.wrongPy: mèi mei le chī bāo zi
items.why: 了 must follow the verb 吃; the correct sentence is 妹妹吃了包子。

items.wrongPy: wǒ shàng le kè zhōng wén
items.why: The object is 中文课, not 课中文; the correct sentence is 我上了中文课。

items.wrongPy: wǒ le kàn jiàn fēi jī
items.why: 了 follows the verb 看见; the correct sentence is 我看见飞机了。

items.wrongPy: wǒ chī le bāo zi yì xiē
items.why: 一些 must precede 包子; the correct order is 我吃了一些包子。

items.wrongPy: zhōng wǔ tā men le chī miàn tiáor
items.why: 了 follows 吃, not the subject; the correct sentence is 中午他们吃了面条儿。

items.note: Place 很 between the subject and an adjective to form a neutral description; it does not necessarily mean very. Learners may put 很 after the adjective, but standard Mandarin requires it before the adjective in this pattern.

items.wrongPy: shū guì hěn
items.why: In this description, 很 comes before 贵, so say 书很贵.

items.en: My younger sister is very young.
items.wrongPy: mèi mei xiǎo hěn
items.why: In this description, 很 comes before 小, so say 妹妹很小.

items.wrongPy: nà li hǎo wánr hěn
items.why: In this description, 很 comes before 好玩儿, so say 那里很好玩儿.

items.en: Those new clothes are very expensive.
items.wrongPy: nà xiē xīn yī fu guì hěn
items.why: In this description, 很 comes before 贵, so say 那些新衣服很贵.

items.note: 没有 negates 有 to express that someone lacks something or that something does not exist in a place or time. Learners often use 不有, but 有 is negated with 没有, not 不有.

items.en: There is no money over there.
items.wrongPy: nà bian bù yǒu qián
items.why: 有 is negated with 没有, so 那边没有钱 is right.

items.wrongPy: nà li bù yǒu yǐ zi
items.why: Use 没有 rather than 不有 to say chairs are absent.

items.en: There is no snow this month.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge yuè bù yǒu xuě
items.why: The negative form of 有 is 没有, so 这个月没有雪 is right.

items.en: I know there is no snow there.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zhī dào nà li bù yǒu xuě
items.why: Use 没有 to negate 有, even inside a sentence after 知道.

items.note: For a year, say each digit in sequence and place 年 after the complete digit string. Learners may insert 年 too early, move it into the sentence, or disturb the digits; doing so changes or breaks the year expression.

items.wrongPy: èr líng nián èr liù wǒ men shàng kè
items.why: 年 must follow the complete year; the correct opening is 二零二六年.

items.phrase: 二零二六年她们都上课
items.zh: 二零二六年她们都上课。
items.wrong: 二零二六都年她们上课。
items.wrongPy: èr líng èr liù dōu nián tā men shàng kè
items.why: 都 cannot split the year from 年; the correct wording is 二零二六年她们都上课.

items.phrase: 二零二六年我们学习汉语
items.zh: 二零二六年我们学习汉语。
items.wrong: 二零二六学习汉语年我们。
items.wrongPy: èr líng èr liù xué xí hàn yǔ nián wǒ men
items.why: 年 must follow the year digits, not the sentence; the correct opening is 二零二六年.

items.phrase: 二零二六年三月十号有雪
items.zh: 二零二六年三月十号有雪。
items.wrong: 二零二六年三月号十有雪。
items.wrongPy: èr líng èr liù nián sān yuè hào shí yǒu xuě
items.why: 号 follows the day number; the correct date is 三月十号.

items.note: Personal pronouns keep the same form as subjects and objects, and they come before their predicates when used as subjects. Put 也 or 都 before the verb phrase; learners often place these adverbs after the verb or before the subject.

items.wrongPy: tā xǐ huan yě xuě
items.why: 也 belongs before 喜欢, so 她也喜欢雪 is right.

items.wrongPy: dōu tā men xǐ huan xuě
items.why: 都 comes after the subject and before 喜欢, so 他们都喜欢雪 is right.

items.en: I know him, and he knows me too.
items.wrongPy: wǒ rèn shi tā tā rèn shi yě wǒ
items.why: 也 comes before the predicate 认识, so 他也认识我 is right.

items.en: I watched a movie last Sunday.
items.wrongPy: shàng xīng qī tiān wǒ le kàn diàn yǐng
items.why: 了 follows the verb 看, so 上星期天我看了电影 is right.

items.note: Chinese time expressions can appear before the subject or after it, as long as they come before the verb phrase. Use this to say when an action happens. Learners often put the time after the action, where it may change the meaning or sound ungrammatical.

items.wrongPy: jīn tiān dōu tā men xiū xi
items.why: 都 must follow the subject and precede the predicate; the correct order is 今天她们都休息。

items.en: I want to learn Chinese next year.
items.wrongPy: míng nián xiǎng wǒ xué zhōng wén
items.why: The subject must precede 想; say 明年我想学中文。

items.en: We are going to see a movie on Sunday.
items.wrongPy: xīng qī tiān wǒ men diàn yǐng qù kàn
items.why: 看 must precede its object 电影; the correct phrase is 星期天我们去看电影。

items.note: Write the year as digits followed by 年, then the cardinal month and day followed by 月 and 日 or 号. Use this for calendar dates; learners often put 月 before the year or use the wrong order.

items.phrase: 二零二六年三月八号有雪
items.zh: 二零二六年三月八号有雪。
items.wrong: 三月二零二六年八号有雪。
items.wrongPy: sān yuè èr líng èr liù nián bā hào yǒu xuě
items.why: The year must come before the month, so the correct form is 二零二六年三月八号。

items.phrase: 二零二六年三月九号有雪
items.zh: 二零二六年三月九号有雪。
items.wrong: 二零二六年九号三月有雪。
items.wrongPy: èr líng èr liù nián jiǔ hào sān yuè yǒu xuě
items.why: The month must come before the day, so the correct form is 二零二六年三月九号。

items.note: Use the negative marker before a verb phrase to say an event did not occur, usually for past events; the shorter form is equivalent to the longer one. Learners often put the marker after the verb or use the wrong kind of negation.

items.wrongPy: wǒ tīng méi jiàn
items.why: 没 must precede the verb phrase 听见, so the correct sentence is 我没听见。

items.en: He didn’t go to see a doctor.
items.wrongPy: tā qù méi kàn bìng
items.why: 没 must precede 去看病, so the correct sentence is 他没去看病。

items.wrongPy: tā chī méi miàn tiáor
items.why: 没 must precede 吃面条儿, so the correct sentence is 她没吃面条儿。

items.wrongPy: zuó tiān wǒ jiàn méi tā men
items.why: 没 must precede 见他们, so the correct sentence is 昨天我没见他们。

items.en: They did not read books yesterday.
items.wrongPy: zuó tiān tā men dú méi yǒu shū
items.why: 没有 must precede 读书, so the correct sentence is 昨天他们没有读书。

items.note: Put a number between the verb and 下 to count brief actions; 一下 can also soften a request. Learners often put the number before the verb or place 下 after the object instead.

items.wrongPy: wǒ sān xià kàn
items.why: The number and 下 follow the verb, so say 我看三下。

items.note: Add 吗 to the end of a statement to make a yes-or-no question, keeping the statement's word order. Do not put 吗 inside the sentence. This pattern is not used with question words or A-not-A questions.

items.wrongPy: ma nǐ zuò fàn
items.why: 吗 must come at the end of the statement; say 你做饭吗？

items.wrongPy: nǐ ma shì lǎo shī
items.why: 吗 belongs after the full statement; say 你是老师吗？

items.wrongPy: nǐ men ma xià bān le
items.why: 吗 must follow 下班了, not interrupt the statement.

items.wrongPy: zhè ge dōng xi ma duì
items.why: 吗 must follow 对; say 这个东西对吗？

items.en: Are you all arriving at school today?
items.wrongPy: nǐ men jīn tiān ma dào xué xiào
items.why: 吗 goes after 到学校, at the end of the question.

items.note: Place the topic before 怎么样 to ask for a description or assessment. Since 怎么样 already forms a question, learners should not add 吗 at the end.

items.wrongPy: zhè biān zěn me yàng ma
items.why: 怎么样 already forms the question, so do not add 吗: 这边怎么样？

items.wrongPy: zhè jiàn shì zěn me yàng ma
items.why: 怎么样 already forms the question, so do not add 吗: 这件事怎么样？

items.note: Put 第 before the number to mark an ordinal, then keep the appropriate measure word between the ordinal and the noun. Use this for numbered days, books, and similar counted things. Learners often omit the measure word after the ordinal.

items.wrongPy: zhè shì tiān dì sān
items.why: The ordinal must come before the noun; the correct order is 第三天.

items.wrongPy: wǒ kàn dì yī shū
items.why: Keep the measure word 本 after 第一; the correct phrase is 第一本书.

items.wrongPy: zhè shì dì èr diàn huà
items.why: Keep the measure word 个 after 第二; the correct phrase is 第二个电话.

items.note: Put 这 or 那 before 是, then use a noun phrase to identify the person or thing being pointed out. Learners often put 是 after the noun phrase; it belongs before it. In some time expressions, such as ordinal days, do not add a measure word.

items.wrongPy: shì zhè wǒ jiā rén
items.why: 是 must follow 这 and precede the noun phrase; it cannot start this identification pattern.

items.wrongPy: zhè shì dì sān gè tiān
items.why: Ordinal day expressions use 天 directly here; adding 个 gives the wrong measure-word pattern.

items.wrongPy: zhè dì èr gè diàn huà shì
items.why: 是 must come before the noun phrase, not after it, in this identification pattern.

items.note: Use 哪 followed by the noun’s measure word and then the noun to ask which one. The question word stays where the answer would go. Learners often put 哪 before the measure word or leave the measure word out.

items.wrongPy: nǐ běn kàn nǎ shū
items.why: 哪本 must stay together before 书; the correct question is 你看哪本书？

items.wrongPy: běn nǎ shū hǎo kàn
items.why: 哪 must come before 本 and 书; the correct question is 哪本书好看？

items.en: Which country do you want to go to?
items.wrongPy: nǐ xiǎng qù nǎ guó jiā
items.why: Keep the measure word 个 after 哪; the correct question is 你想去哪个国家？

items.note: Two related clauses can be placed side by side with a comma, without an explicit connector. Keep each clause’s usual word order; learners often move particles or adverbs inside a clause, or omit a negation that carries its meaning.

items.wrongPy: méi shì nǐ men ba shàng kè
items.why: 吧 belongs after 上课 as a suggestion; the correct clause is 你们上课吧.

items.en: It's okay; we still have class in the afternoon.
items.wrongPy: méi shì xià wǔ shàng kè hái
items.why: 还 must precede 上课; the correct clause is 下午还上课.

items.en: She is ill, so she isn’t working today.
items.wrongPy: tā bìng le jīn tiān gōng zuò
items.why: Omitting 不 reverses the given meaning; the correct clause is 今天不工作.

items.en: After class, I go to a restaurant to eat.
items.wrongPy: xià kè hòu wǒ qù chī fàn fàn diàn
items.why: 饭店 must follow 去 and precede 吃饭; the correct order is 我去饭店吃饭.

items.note: Use 几 before a measure word to ask for a usually small count; use 多少 directly before a noun for an open quantity. Learners often omit the measure word after 几 or put it after the noun.

items.en: How many days do you work?
items.wrongPy: nǐ gōng zuò tiān jǐ
items.why: 几 must come before 天; the correct order is 你工作几天？

items.en: How many cups of tea do you want?
items.wrongPy: nǐ yào bēi duō shao chá
items.why: 多少 comes before 杯茶, not after 杯; say 你要多少杯茶？

items.en: How many friends do you have?
items.wrongPy: nǐ yǒu gè jǐ péng you
items.why: 几 must precede 个, so the correct phrase is 你有几个朋友？

items.en: How many apples do you have?
items.wrongPy: nǐ yǒu jǐ bēi píng guǒ
items.why: 杯 is not the appropriate measure word for counting apples; use 个 in 你有几个苹果？

items.en: How many vegetables does the supermarket sell?
items.wrongPy: duō shao chāo shì mài cài
items.why: 多少 belongs before the quantity noun, not before 超市; say 超市卖多少菜？

items.en: How many hours do you need?
items.wrongPy: nǐ yào xiǎo shí jǐ gè
items.why: 几个 must come before 小时; the correct order is 你要几个小时？

items.note: Put 在 and the place before the verb phrase to say where an action happens. Here 在 marks the action's location, not an ongoing action. Learners often move the place after the verb; keep the location before the action.

items.wrongPy: wǒ gōng sī shàng bān zài
items.why: 在 and the location must come before the action 上班.

items.wrongPy: wǒ zài gōng zuò diàn lǐ
items.why: 店里 is the location and must come before 工作.

items.en: My friend attends class at school.
items.wrongPy: péng you zài shàng kè xué xiào
items.why: 学校 is the location and must come before 上课.

items.en: The female doctor works at the hospital.
items.wrongPy: nǚ yī shēng zài gōng zuò yī yuàn
items.why: 医院 is the location and must come before 工作.

items.note: The progressive marker immediately precedes the verb phrase to show an activity in progress; it is not placed after the verb or object. Learners sometimes confuse this marker with a word that introduces a location.

items.wrongPy: tā zài shū kàn
items.why: The verb 看 must precede its object 书, so the correct phrase is 他在看书。

items.en: He is making a phone call.
items.wrongPy: tā dǎ diàn huà zài
items.why: The progressive marker must precede 打电话, so the correct phrase is 他在打电话。

items.wrongPy: dà jiā chī fàn zhèng zài
items.why: 正在 must precede the verb phrase 吃饭, so the correct sentence is 大家正在吃饭。

items.wrongPy: tā men zhèng zài diàn yǐng kàn
items.why: 看 must precede its object 电影, so the correct sentence is 他们正在看电影。

items.note: 在 or 正在 comes before a verb phrase to show an activity in progress, and 呢 usually comes at the end for emphasis. Learners may move 在 or 呢 into the verb phrase; this pattern describes ongoing action, not static possession.

items.en: The dog is sleeping right now.
items.wrongPy: gǒu shuì jiào zhèng zài ne
items.why: 正在 must come before 睡觉; say 狗正在睡觉呢。

items.wrongPy: wài bian xià xuě zhèng zài ne
items.why: 正在 must precede 下雪; say 外边正在下雪呢。

items.en: I’m on the phone with him right now.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zhèng zài gěi dǎ diàn huà tā ne
items.why: 他 must follow 给 in 给他打电话; say 我正在给他打电话呢。

items.note: Sentence-final 了 marks a new or changed situation, such as a condition becoming true now. Use it to present the update, not simply as a past-tense marker. Learners often put 了 before the verb or assume it always means “already.”

items.wrongPy: tā le shēng bìng
items.why: 了 cannot go between the subject and predicate here; the correct sentence is 他生病了。

items.note: Use 元 or 块 for whole yuan, and 分 for hundredths of a yuan; the amount comes before its unit. Learners may mistake 分 for a whole-yuan unit or put a remainder after 元 instead of before it.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yǒu wǔ bǎi fēn
items.why: 五百分 is five yuan, not five hundred yuan; say 我有五百元。

items.wrongPy: sān qiān wǔ yuán
items.why: 三千五元 means 3,500 yuan, not 3,005; say 三千零五元。

items.en: This book costs three thousand yuan.
items.wrongPy: zhè běn shū sān qiān fēn
items.why: 三千分 is 30 yuan, not 3,000; say 这本书三千元。

items.en: There are seven hundred yuan there.
items.wrongPy: nàr yǒu qī bǎi fēn
items.why: 七百分 is seven yuan, not seven hundred yuan; say 那儿有七百元。

items.en: There are three yuan on this side.
items.wrongPy: zhè biān yǒu sān kuài fēn
items.why: 块 and 分 cannot be stacked this way as one unit; say 这边有三块钱。

items.wrongPy: shǒu jī mài sān qiān yuán wǔ
items.why: The remainder must come before 元; say 手机卖三千零五元。

items.note: Form this yes-or-no question by repeating the predicate with 不 between the two copies; do not add 吗. It works with verbs and adjectives, and learners often add 吗 as if using a regular question.

items.wrongPy: nǐ shàng bú shàng kè ma
items.why: The A-not-A form already makes a question, so omit 吗: 你上不上课？

items.en: Are there many people in the shop?
items.wrongPy: diàn lǐ rén duō bù duō ma
items.why: The A-not-A form already makes a question, so omit 吗: 店里人多不多？

items.note: 能 and 可以 come before a verb phrase: 能 often expresses ability or circumstances, while 可以 often asks for or gives permission, or expresses possibility. Learners may put the modal after the verb; keep it before the whole verb phrase.

items.wrongPy: tā dú néng hàn zì
items.why: 能 must come before the verb phrase; say 她能读汉字。

items.en: My older sister can listen to songs.
items.wrongPy: jiě jie néng gē tīng
items.why: 听歌 is the verb phrase, so 能 must precede it; say 姐姐能听歌。

items.wrongPy: tā men kāi néng chē
items.why: 能 must precede the verb 开车; say 他们能开车。

items.en: May I listen to a song?
items.wrongPy: wǒ tīng kě yǐ gē ma
items.why: 可以 must come before the verb phrase 听歌; say 我可以听歌吗？

items.wrongPy: nǐ zuò kě yǐ zhèr ma
items.why: 可以 must precede the verb phrase 坐这儿; say 你可以坐这儿吗？

items.phrase: 我们可以在这里听歌吗
items.zh: 我们可以在这里听歌吗？
items.en: May we listen to music here?
items.wrong: 我们可以在这里歌听吗？
items.wrongPy: wǒ men kě yǐ zài zhè lǐ gē tīng ma
items.why: The verb phrase is 听歌, not 歌听; say 我们可以在这里听歌吗？

items.note: 也 means “also” or “too” and normally comes after the subject but before the predicate it modifies. It can modify a whole predicate, including a verb with its object. Learners often put 也 between a verb and its object; keep it before the predicate instead.

items.wrongPy: tā chī yě cài
items.why: 也 cannot split the verb from its object here; say 他也吃菜.

items.wrongPy: tā dú yě shū
items.why: 也 cannot split the verb from its object here; say 她也读书.

items.wrongPy: tā mǎi yě jī dàn
items.why: 也 cannot split the verb from its object here; say 他也买鸡蛋.

items.wrongPy: tā xǐ huan yě xuě
items.why: 也 cannot split the verb from its object here; say 她也喜欢雪.

items.en: Xiao Wang is also at the shop.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo wáng zài yě diàn lǐ
items.why: 也 must come before the predicate 在店里; say 小王也在店里.

items.note: Use 在 before a place to say where a person or thing is located. This pattern describes a location, not an action taking place there. Learners often put the place before 在; keep 在 between the subject and the place.

items.wrongPy: tā men jiā zài
items.why: 在 must come before 家; the place cannot follow 在 in this pattern.

items.wrongPy: gǒu zhèr zài
items.why: 这儿 must follow 在, not come before it.

items.wrongPy: diàn nǎo nàr zài
items.why: 那儿 must follow 在, not come before it.

items.en: The money is under the chair.
items.wrongPy: qián yǐ zi xià zài
items.why: 在 must come before the place 椅子下.

items.en: Xiao Wang is also at the shop.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo wáng zài yě diàn lǐ
items.why: 也 must come before 在; it cannot split 在 from the place.

items.en: Some cats are behind the table.
items.wrongPy: yǒu de māo zhuō zi hòu biān zài
items.why: 在 must come before the place 桌子后边.

items.note: Put a direction word before 边 to name a location, as in 右边 or 前边. Learners often reverse the order and put 边 before the direction word.

items.en: The cat is beside the table.
items.wrongPy: māo zài biān zhuō zi
items.why: Put 桌子 before 边; the correct location phrase is 桌子边。

items.wrongPy: biān qián shì fēi jī
items.why: The direction word 前 precedes 边; the correct phrase is 前边是飞机。

items.en: There is a shop in front of the restaurant.
items.wrongPy: fàn diàn biān qián shì shāng diàn
items.why: Put 前 before 边; the correct sentence is 饭店前边是商店。

items.note: Put the weekday name immediately after the weekday marker: the numbers from one through six name Monday through Saturday, and the two words for seven mean Sunday. Learners may mistakenly separate the number from the marker.

items.wrongPy: xīng qī wǒ men sān shàng kè
items.why: The weekday number must immediately follow the marker, so the correct sentence is 星期三我们上课。

items.wrongPy: xīng qī tā men sì dú shū
items.why: The weekday number must immediately follow the marker, so the correct sentence is 星期四他们读书。

items.note: Place 半 before the measure word and noun to express half of one counted item or amount. Use the measure word required by the noun. Learners often omit that word or repeat it by mistake.

items.wrongPy: wǒ yào bàn gè gè bāo zi
items.why: Use only one measure word 个; the correct phrase is 半个包子.

items.wrongPy: wǒ mǎi bàn gè gè píng guǒ
items.why: Use only one measure word 个; the correct phrase is 半个苹果.

items.note: Use one 零 to bridge skipped place values when a higher place is followed by a lower nonzero place. Do not add a trailing zero. Learners often omit the bridge or repeat 零.

items.wrongPy: sān qiān líng líng wǔ yuán
items.why: Use only one 零 as the bridge; the correct amount is 三千零五元.

items.wrongPy: shǒu jī mài sān qiān wǔ yuán
items.why: Without 零, 三千五 means 3,500, not 3,005; the correct amount is 三千零五元.

items.note: A preposition such as 在 or 离 comes before its object, and the resulting phrase gives a location or distance relation. Use it before the main predicate or distance description; learners often put the object after the verb or place 离 after 很近.

items.wrongPy: wǒ zài chī fàn fàn diàn
items.why: 饭店 must follow 在 as its object, not come after 吃饭; say 我在饭店吃饭.

items.wrongPy: wǒ zài dú shū jiā lǐ
items.why: 家里 is the object of 在 and must precede 读书; say 我在家里读书.

items.note: A transitive verb comes before the thing it acts on, including a noun phrase with a number and measure word. Use this order for actions such as cooking, wearing, or drinking. Learners often place the object before the verb or put the measure word after the noun.

items.wrongPy: zuò nǐ fàn ma
items.why: The subject 你 must precede 做 and its object 饭; the correct question is 你做饭吗？

items.wrongPy: kàn zhè ge yí kàn
items.why: The one-time reduplication 一看 belongs immediately after 看; say 看一看这个。

items.en: My younger sister wears new clothes.
items.wrongPy: mèi mei chuān yī fu xīn
items.why: The modifier 新 must precede 衣服; the correct order is 妹妹穿新衣服。

items.en: They drink five cups of milk.
items.wrongPy: tā men hē wǔ gè niú nǎi
items.why: 个 is not the measure word used for milk here; the phrase uses 五杯牛奶。

items.note: Put 小 directly before a surname as a familiar form of address, often for someone younger. It is not a general diminutive to place before any given name; learners also sometimes reverse 小 and the surname.

items.wrongPy: xiǎo zài wáng zhèr
items.why: 小 must directly precede the surname 王; it cannot be separated from it by 在.

items.wrongPy: xiǎo míng tiān wáng lái
items.why: 小 must attach directly to 王 as a familiar surname form; it cannot be separated from the surname.

items.en: Xiao Wang is also at the shop.
items.wrongPy: yě xiǎo wáng zài diàn lǐ
items.why: 也 normally precedes the verb phrase 在店里, not the subject 小王.

items.en: Can I ask Xiao Wang to come?
items.wrongPy: wǒ kě yǐ xiǎo wáng jiào lái ma
items.why: 叫 must precede its object 小王; the correct order is 可以叫小王来.

items.note: A location phrase followed by 是 plus a noun phrase identifies what is at that location. Use this to identify or locate something; learners often put 在 before 是 or confuse this pattern with 有.

items.wrongPy: qián biān zài shì fēi jī
items.why: 在 cannot be inserted before 是 in this identifying pattern; the correct order is 前边是飞机.

items.en: There is a shop in front of the restaurant.
items.wrongPy: fàn diàn qián biān zài shì shāng diàn
items.why: 在 cannot come between the location phrase and 是; say 饭店前边是商店.

items.note: For these duration expressions, place a number directly before 年, 天, or 分; do not insert 个 with these units. Use the resulting time phrase for a length of time or a time interval; learners often overgeneralize 个 from other measure words.

items.wrongPy: tā gōng zuò sān gè tiān
items.why: 天 takes the number directly here, without 个; the correct duration is 三天.

items.en: It will snow in three days.
items.wrongPy: sān gè tiān hòu xià xuě
items.why: 天 takes the number directly in this time expression; say 三天后, not 三个天后.

items.en: I’m staying in China for two days.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zài zhōng guó zhù liǎng gè tiān
items.why: Use 两天 without 个 for this duration; 两个天 is not the standard measure phrase.

items.note: This pattern links two actions performed by the same subject, often with the first action leading to or making the second possible. Use it for sequences and purposes without adding a conjunction. Learners often reverse the order or insert a particle between the actions.

items.en: I’m going to meet Xiao Wang.
items.wrongPy: qù wǒ jiàn xiǎo wáng
items.why: The subject must come before the actions; the correct order is subject, first action, then purpose action.

items.en: I go to a restaurant to eat.
items.wrongPy: wǒ qù chī fàn fàn diàn
items.why: The destination belongs after the movement verb and before the purpose action, not after it.

items.note: 请 comes before a verb phrase to make a polite request. Use it to invite or ask someone to do something, often with 吧 for a softer tone. Learners may put 请 after the verb or move a sentence-final particle into the phrase.

items.wrongPy: tīng qǐng gē
items.why: 请 must come before the verb phrase; the correct request is 请听歌。

items.en: Please get out of the vehicle.
items.wrongPy: qǐng chē xià
items.why: 下车 is the verb phrase and cannot be reversed here; the correct request is 请下车。

items.wrongPy: qǐng míng zi xiě
items.why: 请 must precede the verb phrase 写名字; the correct request is 请写名字。

items.wrongPy: qǐng diàn shì kāi
items.why: 开电视 is the verb phrase and cannot be reversed here; the correct request is 请开电视。

items.wrongPy: qǐng yí xià zuò
items.why: 一下 follows the verb 做; the correct request is 请做一下。

items.wrongPy: qǐng ba chī miàn bāo
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end of the request; the correct order is 请吃面包吧。

items.note: Put 吧 at the end of a suggestion or softened request to invite agreement. It can make an instruction sound less direct. Learners sometimes place 吧 after the subject or in the middle of the sentence; keep it after the whole suggestion.

items.wrongPy: qǐng ba chī miàn bāo
items.why: 吧 follows the whole softened request; the correct wording is 请吃面包吧。

items.en: Come over and find me soon.
items.wrongPy: kuài ba guò lái zhǎo wǒ
items.why: 吧 cannot interrupt this request; the correct wording is 快过来找我吧。

items.wrongPy: jīn tiān ba wǒ men zuò fàn
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end, not after 今天; the correct suggestion is 今天我们做饭吧。

items.en: It’s okay; you all go rest.
items.wrongPy: méi guān xi nǐ men ba xiū xi
items.why: 吧 follows the complete request to rest; the correct sentence is 没关系，你们休息吧。

items.note: Place the possessor before the noun and link them with 的. 的 can be omitted in some close family relationships, as in 我男朋友, but learners should not omit it freely with other nouns or move it away from the possessor.

items.wrongPy: tā shū hěn xīn
items.why: 她 is not a close-family term here, so the possessive needs 的; say 她的书很新。

items.wrongPy: tā men de hěn hǎo tīng gē
items.why: 她们的歌 must stay together, with 的 directly before 歌; say 她们的歌很好听。

items.wrongPy: wǒ de zài zhèr xìng míng
items.why: 我的 must directly modify 姓名; say 我的姓名在这儿。

items.wrongPy: tā shì nǚ péng you wǒ de
items.why: 我的 must precede 女朋友 rather than follow it; say 她是我的女朋友。

items.note: A location word such as 上, 里, or 后 follows the noun it locates, as in 椅子上 and 房间里. Learners may put the location word before the noun; keep the noun first, then add the appropriate location word.

items.en: There is a bus stop behind the pharmacy.
items.wrongPy: yào diàn yǒu hòu mian chē zhàn
items.why: 后面 must follow 药店 to locate the车站; say 药店后面有车站。

items.en: One person is missing from the restaurant.
items.wrongPy: fàn diàn shǎo lǐ yí gè rén
items.why: 里 follows 饭店 to mark the location; say 饭店里少一个人。

items.note: Add 们 to a personal pronoun or a human noun to mark a plural group. It is not used with ordinary numbered noun phrases. Learners may attach it to the wrong word; it follows the person it pluralizes.

items.wrongPy: tā men zài chē zhàn děng men
items.why: 们 must follow the personal pronoun, not the verb; say 他们在车站等。

items.wrongPy: tā men zài dà xué men zhù
items.why: 们 does not pluralize 大学 here; say 他们在大学住。

items.wrongPy: tā men dōu xǐ huan xuě men
items.why: 们 cannot mark 雪 as a plural human group; say 他们都喜欢雪。

items.wrongPy: xīng qī sì tā men dú shū men
items.why: 们 must follow the human pronoun, not 读书; say 星期四他们读书。

items.wrongPy: tā men zhèng zài kàn diàn yǐng men
items.why: 们 cannot pluralize 电影; say 他们正在看电影。

items.note: A place expression such as 这儿 or 那里 can stand before a predicate to say what is true there. In location sentences, learners may put 在 before the thing located instead of after it, as in 本子在里面.

items.wrongPy: lǐ miàn zài běn zi
items.why: The thing located comes before 在, so 本子在里面 is right.

items.en: There is no money over there.
items.wrongPy: nà bian bù yǒu qián
items.why: 有 is negated with 没有, so 那边没有钱 is right.

items.en: It’s a lot of fun here.
items.wrongPy: zhèr hǎo wánr hěn
items.why: 很 goes before the descriptive predicate, so 这儿很好玩儿 is right.

items.wrongPy: nà li hǎo wánr hěn
items.why: 很 comes before 好玩儿, so 那里很好玩儿 is right.

items.note: Use a location phrase first, then 有, then the thing that exists; a quantity phrase may go before the noun but is optional. Learners often put 有 after the noun or stack two classifiers before it.

items.en: There is a shop over there.
items.wrongPy: nà bian yǒu yì jiā gè diàn
items.why: 家 already measures 店, so adding 个 creates an invalid double classifier.

items.en: There is a packet of green tea inside.
items.wrongPy: lǐ miàn yì bāo yǒu lǜ chá
items.why: The quantity phrase and noun must follow 有, so 里面有一包绿茶 is right.

items.note: Put 多 before a gradable adjective to ask about degree or measurement, such as height or size. 有 may optionally appear before 多. Learners often put 多 after the adjective, but that reverses the question pattern.

items.wrongPy: zhè lóu gāo duō
items.why: 多 must precede 高; the correct question is 这楼多高？

items.wrongPy: nà lóu yǒu gāo duō
items.why: 多 must precede 高; the correct question is 那楼有多高？

items.wrongPy: nǐ de fáng jiān dà duō
items.why: 多 must precede 大; the correct question is 你的房间多大？

items.wrongPy: zhè ge fàn diàn dà duō
items.why: 多 must precede 大; the correct question is 这个饭店多大？

items.note: 在 can introduce a time or place before the action, as in 在星期日上课 or 在车站送我. Learners may omit 在 when it is needed to mark the location, or confuse 后 in 下课后 with other position words.

items.en: He sees me off at the station.
items.wrongPy: tā chē zhàn sòng wǒ
items.why: 车站 needs 在 to mark where he sees me off; say 他在车站送我。

items.en: Everyone goes to the shop after class.
items.wrongPy: dà jiā zài xià kè lǐ qù diàn lǐ
items.why: 里 cannot replace 后 in 下课后, which means “after class”; say 大家在下课后去店里。
